tldr: Anthropic published Fable 5's cyber classifiers and a first jailbreak severity framework on Jul 2, setting out the model's early safety posture. Two weeks later, Anthropic confirmed Fable 5 access becomes a permanent part of Max and Team Premium plans.
whats_new: Fable 5 becomes a permanent part of Max and Team Premium plans starting Jul 20, at 50% of prior limits — Pro and Team Standard users keep more limited access.
why_it_matters: Locking in Fable 5 as a permanent (if reduced-limit) benefit gives Max/Team Premium teams continuity of access even as GPT-5.6 Sol and Moonshot's Kimi K3 court agentic-coding workloads — teams on Pro or Team Standard should confirm their tier still covers the usage they need.

status.state: Permanent · Max/Team Premium, 50% of prior limits
status.detail: Fable 5 access moves to a permanent part of Max and Team Premium plans (at 50% of prior limits) starting Jul 20; Pro and Team Standard users keep more limited access.

beats.headline: Anthropic details Fable 5's cyber classifiers and a first jailbreak severity framework
beats.summary: What is and isn't blocked by the cyber classifiers, plus a first draft of a jailbreak severity framework — the model's early safety posture.

beats.headline: Fable 5 becomes a permanent Max/Team Premium benefit, at 50% of prior limits
beats.summary: Anthropic confirms Fable 5 will be included in all Max and Team Premium plans beginning Jul 20, at 50% of prior limits; Pro and Team Standard users keep more limited access.

open_questions: Do Pro and Team Standard plans get any expanded Fable 5 access, or does the permanent benefit stay limited to Max/Team Premium?
Does the 50%-of-limits cap change as competitive pressure from GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi K3 continues?
Does Anthropic publish further detail on the cyber classifiers/jailbreak severity framework from the Jul 2 post, or does it stay a one-off disclosure?
take_for_builders: If your team is on Max or Team Premium, confirm your workflows fit inside the 50%-of-prior-limits cap before relying on Fable 5 as a permanent fixture; Pro/Team Standard users should check whether their current access still covers agentic-coding workloads now that competitors are courting that use case.
